pages.text: Information takes room. Bekenstein's bound says an object of radius R and energy E holds at most S = 2πRE/(ħc·ln 2) bits - so the densest things need the most energy in the least space. But squeeze energy E inside its Schwarzschild radius 2GE/c⁴ and it becomes a black hole. The richest forgings sit just outside that edge.
$(thing)Set$(): Field energy (log₁₀ J), Forging radius (log₁₀ m).$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The vacuum fluctuates: the energy actually held varies by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The forging volume is collapsing behind its own horizon; The Foundry is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The more room the bound leaves above what the forging needs, the faster it goes.
